\\n\\ud83d\\udcdd Walkthrough\\n\\n## Walkthrough\\n\\nAdds combo rarity, unlock cost, and level progression to combos; new ScriptableObjects and editor tooling for rarity data; Memory gains unlock/level persistence helpers; UI updated to render locked/special combos via a new SpecialComboCell and rarity visuals.\\n\\n## Changes\\n\\n|Cohort / File(s)|Summary|\\n|---|---|\\n|**Core Combo Definition**
`Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboDefinition.cs`|Added `ERarityEnum` (Common, Rare, Epic, Legendary, Mythic), `UnlockCost`, `Rarity`, `LevelMultipliers`, and computed properties `Locked`, `Level`, `MaxLevel` backed by `Memory` helpers.|\\n|**Rarity Data Infrastructure**
`Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboRarityData.cs`, `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboRarityDefinition.cs`, `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/ComboCellRarityData.cs`|New ScriptableObjects: `ComboRarityData` (singleton, editor FillComboRarities), `ComboRarityDefinition` (level requirements), and `CombosCellRarityData`/`ComboCellRarityData` (rarity display data and reset on load).|\\n|**Memory Persistence**
`Assets/Scripts/Helper/Memory.cs`|Added `IsComboUnlocked`, `UnlockCombo`, `GetComboLevel`, and `IncreaseComboLevel` to persist and query combo unlock state and levels.|\\n|**UI & Cells**
`Assets/Scripts/UI/ComboScreen.cs`, `Assets/Scripts/UI/SpecialComboCell.cs`|`ComboScreen` conditionally instantiates a `SpecialComboCell` for locked or non-Common combos; `LockedComboCell` renamed/refactored to `SpecialComboCell`, uses a `SerializedDictionary` for visuals, handles unlock flow and currency updates.|\\n|**Assets / Meta**
`Assets/Resources/Combos/*`, `Assets/Scripts/ScriptableObjects/*.meta`, `Assets/Resources/Combos/*.asset.meta`, `Assets/Art/Textures/UI/*.meta`|Added folder/meta entries and asset meta files for rarity assets and new scriptable object meta files; new texture meta entries for rare backgrounds/frames.|\\n\\n## Sequence Diagram\\n\\n```mermaid\\nsequenceDiagram\\n participant ComboScreen as ComboScreen\\n participant ComboDefinition as ComboDefinition\\n participant Memory as Memory\\n participant SpecialComboCell as SpecialComboCell\\n participant RarityData as CombosCellRarityData\\n\\n ComboScreen->>ComboDefinition: read Locked, Rarity\\n ComboDefinition->>Memory: IsComboUnlocked(name)\\n Memory-->>ComboDefinition: unlocked/locked\\n\\n alt Locked or Rarity != Common\\n ComboScreen->>SpecialComboCell: Instantiate _specialPrefab\\n SpecialComboCell->>ComboDefinition: evaluate Locked\\n alt Locked\\n SpecialComboCell->>RarityData: request visuals for Rarity\\n RarityData-->>SpecialComboCell: return sprites/text\\n SpecialComboCell->>Memory: UnlockCombo(name) [on user action]\\n Memory-->>SpecialComboCell: persist result\\n else Unlocked (special)\\n SpecialComboCell->>RarityData: request visuals for Rarity\\n RarityData-->>SpecialComboCell: return sprites/text\\n end\\n else Common & Unlocked\\n ComboScreen->>ComboScreen: Instantiate regular cell and add to list\\n end\\n```\\n\\n## Estimated Code Review Effort\\n\\n\\ud83c\\udfaf 3 (Moderate) | \\u23f1\\ufe0f ~22 minutes\\n\\n## Poem\\n\\n> \\ud83d\\udc30 I munched the code in twilight's glow, \\n> > Rarities shimmer, seeds now sow, \\n> > Locks click open with a little clack, \\n> > Multipliers hop the damage track, \\n> > A rabbit cheers \\u2014 combos on the go!\\n\\n
\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n---\\n\\n> [!NOTE]\\n>

content.text:
Owen Baker is confirmed (owen.baker@harmonygames.co). In PR #37 the author **PERSON_5877** cited "Combo Unlocking Specs" while defending the `ComboRarityDefinition` — that matches Owen's "I pointed at a spec during one of those reviews." Now let me verify what actually shipped vs. the objections, and read the design spec. Key finds for #35: Oliver asked to rename `DominoPlayerPrefs.cs` (Arthur said "Yes") + flagged a dangerous `_statPrefab` pattern; Arthur merged his own PR 6 min later.

Let me pull the shipped file states and the design spec.

Major findings. Let me decode:

**PR #37 (shipped `ComboRarityDefinition.cs`):** the class the author defended by citing the "Combo Unlocking Specs" shipped as just `public int LevelRequirements;` — a bare int stub, NOT the per-rarity/per-level requirement table (Common 100/200/300, Rare 150/300/450) the author described in review. Meanwhile `ComboDefinition.cs` shows Oliver's structural asks *were* mostly applied (enum→`ERarityEnum`, `Locked` now computed via `ComboManager`, row-class gone). Also note: `Common` was dropped from the rarity enum entirely.

**PR #35:** the `DominoPlayerPrefs` rename Arthur agreed to *did* land (now `HarmonyPlayerPrefs.cs`), but Oliver's `_statPrefab` type-safety objection did **not** — still `GameObject` + `GetComponent`, and debug `Debug.Log` calls shipped.

Now let me read the design spec tabs and confirm the AWS/security state, plus sweep the remaining reviewed PRs.

The design spec confirms a key finding: the master **"Combo Fighter Design Details"** spreadsheet (Combo Sheet + Combo List tabs) contains combo definitions and DPS multipliers but **no rarity tiers and no per-level "unlock requirement" table** (no Common 100/200/300, Rare 150/300/450). Let me confirm against the GDD and Confluence, and set up the Linear side (engineering board + Zombie Match).

{"mimeType": "text/markdown", "text": "Overview

### 1. Game Overview
Title: Combo Fighter
Genre: Merge puzzle auto battler
Platform: (iOS / Android)
Core Loop Summary:
Place fight-action tetris shaped pieces on a game board and watch the character fight hordes of enemies.
### 2. Core Gameplay
Player Actions:
Drag tetris shaped pieces onto the game board, merge pieces to upgrade them, connect the pieces to create combos to deal extra damage, fill the board with more pieces to deal more attacks and/or damage.
Draw additional pieces randomly to place them on the board. Optimize your spaces and combo connections.
Gain experience by defeating monsters and merging tiles. Experience levels up the hero and the player can choose a skill upgrade.
When the game ends, the player can upgrade the hero's Max HP, HP regen rate during the game, and attack power.
Game Objective:
Defeat all the waves of monsters in each level.
Failure Condition:
The player’s HP reaches 0 from monster attacks.
### 3. Game Flow
Home Screen: Start button, current level displayed, three upgrade buttons.
Gameplay: 4 to 5 minutes per level. The game switches from preparation phase to battle phase with occasional pop up dialogue for roguelite skill upgrades.
Result Screen: Displays rewards earned. Gold only in MVP.
Upgrades: Hero’s Max HP, HP regen rate, hero’s attack power bonus
### 4. Level Design
35 hand crafted levels in MVP
Monsters will have increased HP and attack damage as level progresses.
Levels will have obstacles on the board to create difficulty. These obstacles can be removed with silver earned in the level. These obstacles reset each game.
Levels will have different starting points for first combo piece placement. Each level will also have a set of possible pieces that can be dropped and their drop rate.
### 5. Art & Visual Style
The top portion of the screen is dedicated to combat visualization during battle phase, the bottom portion only displays the puzzle board.
During intermission between waves of monsters, the camera shifts down to reveal a puzzle board + three slots staging area for players to obtain new puzzle pieces, this is the preparation phase. Pressing a FIGHT button will shift the camera back up and transition into the battle phase.
Character Designs: Simple Chibi style 3D characters.
UI: Simple standard UI, home screen with minimal buttons.
### 6. Audio
Music: None
SFX: Standard fighting sounds.
### 7. Monetization
Ads: None in MVP
### 8. Ugly Game Mockups
Home Screen with 3 upgrade choices, start button, coin balance and settings button

Gameplay

Game Starts, 3 pieces randomly selected for players to choose from.
Players drag pieces onto the board, the character starts doing loop animation of the attacks on the board.
The values showing total punch, kick and special attack power changes real time based on pieces on the board
The dmg/s calculation also updates real time as pieces are being placed
The Info button will bring up a pop up of available moves (see below)
Pressing refresh will consume gold if available, and refreshes the 3 cards.
Holding a tile under the finger will change the refresh button to SELL. If a player moves pieces over the sell button, the piece will be sold.
Coin balance and health is displayed near the top
After pressing the fight button, the camera shifts upward to increase the size of the fight scene and the battle starts. This phase requires no input action from the players
Info Pop Up

Simple End Game Screen


DOCUMENT DOES NOT END HERE! MAKE SURE TO CLICK ON THE OTHER TABS (“Detailed Mechanics”) IN THIS DOCUMENT ON THE LEFT SIDE BAR IN GOOGLE DOCS


Detailed Mechanics
### 1. Starting A Level
Level starts with a 6x6 empty game board.
The level designer will indicate which left most square tile will be the first tile that starts the combo, if tiles are not placed here, There are no combos and only Singular attacks.

Players are presented with a staging area with 3 random tiles at start. They can use these tiles on their board or sell them, or they can press the refresh button which costs silver to be dealt three more random tiles. Pressing the fight buttons begins the battle phase. The tiles themselves are free, only refresh costs money.

Tiles that remain on the board when the refresh button is pressed are sold automatically for 10 gold each.
Once the battle phase starts, the character automatically executes the fighting sequence based on the tiles placed. The enemies will approach from the right side of the screen. If combos are not present on the board, then the player will perform one attack each of punch and/or kicks and/or special attacks if those action tiles exist. There is a 0.6 seconds delay between these attack animations, and these tiles that are not part of the combo will have an attack power penalty. So for example if a combo does not exist, but There are P K and S tiles on the board, the player will do Punch (basic jab animation) → 0.6 second delay → Kick (basic roundhouse kick animation) → 0.6 second delay → Special attack (fireball) → 0.6 second delay → repeat

When the monster crosses the green line seen below, the character will automatically execute the fighting combo. When the monster crosses the red line, they will start to attack the player.

If There are no monsters within melee range of the player, the player will execute a ranged attack based on the total special attack power, with a 0.8 seconds delay between each attack. (Fireball Hadouken animation)

Fireball will hit 3 enemies before disappearing. This can be upgraded. So in this case we can upgrade a fireball to hit the left most 6 enemies.
Players will gain experience and silver from killing monsters. Experience will allow the player to level up within the game and select some random upgrades. Silver is used to obtain more tiles during the preparation phase.

When the wave of monsters is defeated, the camera shifts back down exposing the staging area and we are back to the preparation phase where players get to acquire more tiles and optimize their placements on the board. The game ends in a loss if the player is defeated and HP reaches 0.
The game ends in victory if the player defeats all waves of monsters.
PLEASE NOTE THAT THE AMOUNT OF SILVER AND EXP RECEIVED IS NOT BASED ON MONSTER TYPE KILLED OR QUANTITY OF MONSTERS KILLED. Instead, we are introducing a system that allows designers to set the amount of exp and silver a player will receive each wave, and we divide that across the monsters in that wave..

#### Block Merging & Rearrangement
When the preparation phase starts, There will be 3 blocks spawned in the bottom area to place or merge.
Holding a piece will show possible placements with highlighted corners.
When the tiles have mergeable counterparts in the board, the mergeable tile on the board will have a glowing outline.
Like the video below.
ScreenRecording_11-11-2025 16-11-07_1.MP4
While arranging the placement of blocks, players can move board tiles to the bottom area and rearrange them back and forth.
The only limitation is that 3 blocks can be stored on the bottom part.
Once players decide to continue fighting, clicking the “Fight” button, the pieces left on the bottom would be sold automatically.
Players can merge the blocks in the bottom part.
### 2. Combat Power and Damage Calculation
There are three types of action tiles: Punch (P), Kick (K) and Special Attack (S). The corresponding tile colors are green, blue, and red.

Tiles will display the full combat power they provide. Not penalized discounted power.

Tiles will come in different shapes

Punch has a base attack power of 10, Kick is 20, and Special Attack is 40

The same tiles can be merged and upgraded to increase their power. Tiles that are not part of a combo and only contribute half power are called “Assist Tiles,” they are dimmed visually. When merged it simply sums the combat power. So level 1 Punch = 10, level 2 punch = 20, level 3 punch = 40 (Requires 2x level 2) They do not need to be connected to any pieces to contribute. They just need to be on the board.

The individual power of the combo is shown in the UI like seen here below.



The damage per attack sequence is based on the only combo on the board, each board can only have a max of one combo, and for each action in the combo, the damage dealt is calculated using the following:

[Action Power] = [Tile Power + (50%*(SUM of assist tile power))] * Combo Bonus Multiplier
This calculates the individual action power for the combo

Combo multipliers are pre-assigned by game designers. Here is an example of a combo calculation.



Small sample list of combos and their multiplier and base DPS, this is accessed via the info button during the game. The character at the top animates the combo punching air/dummy when the player selects a combo.



### 3. Combo Creation UI/UX




### 4. Game Currencies and Homescreen Upgrades
There will be 3 different upgradeable stats at the home screen which are persistent across sessions and levels. The currency used to upgrade is gold. We can consider adding an ad watch when players run out of gold.
They will be extended with gears or other upgrades that we can use later on. So for the implementation, please be aware that we can extend upgrades.
Attack Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) So 100% + 2% + 2% + 2% + 2% (Level 4 = 108% * attack)
Health Increase (+2% per upgrade. Additive) Same as attack. So level 5 health increase = 110% * base HP of 100 = 110 total Hp
Health Regen Increase (+0.02% per second, Additive) So level 7 is 2% base regen + (0.02% * 7 = 0.14%) final health regen = 2.14% HP regen per second.
### 5. Monsters, Stats, Damage Assignment, Stagger and Loot
Each monster when hit is “stunned” for 0.25 seconds. However this has a cooldown of 1.5 seconds. This means after being stunned, the earliest the next time the same monster can be stunned again is 1.25 seconds later because 1.5 second cooldown from first stun - 0.25 stun duration = 1.25 seconds after end of first stun.
Monster attack animation should be from start to finish should be 1 second, with damage dealt at 0.8 second timestamp
We do not need more than 5 monsters for MVP
When monsters are hit, we display damage dealt using standard RPG text VFX. We then display the monster health bar permanently above their head, but we do not display numerical values for their HP
Monster speed is the second it takes to move from edge of screen to crossing the monster attack line. Attack speed is expressed in seconds per attack.


### 6. Levels
We need to let designers designate starting positions for each level.
Each level will also have obstacles that need to be removed via silver.

Each level will have 15 waves of monsters
Each wave of monsters will get an HP and damage multiplier bonus following a standard algorithm
HP multiplier for monster is wave # * XXX
Damage multiplier for monster is wave # * YYY
We need to utilize the monster spawning system from Zombie Match, this will allow designers to specify monsters spawn timing and quantity
#### Level Design Tools
Each level will have monsters, monsters spawn, their stats, board type, and the pool of tiles available.

  * `card_level`
    * `0` = Not owned / Locked

  * `timestamp` of the login

#### **2. BigQuery Sync:**

* Send this card inventory data to **BigQuery once per day**, ideally on first login of the day.

* Create a **separate BigQuery table** mapping `card_id` → `card_name` (or human-readable identifier).

`card_id (int) card_name (string)`

input.title: Combo-Fighters PR #26 merged with reviewer's ad-cooldown exploit objection unresolved
input.description:
Record of PR state (Combo Fighter is live). Recorded during the Feb 2026 pre-shutdown audit — unassigned by design; this is a record of state, not a commitment to fix.

**PR:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters #26 "Added cooldown to main menu upgrade ad watch" (author PERSON_5877, merged by Oliver Brooks 2026-01-15).

**Reviewer:** Oliver Brooks — review state CHANGES_REQUESTED. He never re-reviewed or approved before merge.

**What the reviewer objected to (with substance):**
Oliver's review body proposed the 5-min time cooldown but explicitly flagged an exploit: *"the player can enter the level, lose very quickly and return to main menu and then they will be able to watch another ad and level up again."* The cooldown is reset both on level completion AND on the lose screen (`GameController.cs` + `LoseScreen.cs` call `Memory.SetUpgradeAdWatchedCooldown(reset: true)`).

**What actually landed:** The shipped code still resets the cooldown on losing, so the exploit Oliver described is present in the build people are playing. The author deferred to a teammate (EMPLOYEE_0016, "does not matter if the player win or lose... we should sync") and merged without resolution. The minor inline nits (moving Memory helpers) were resolved.

**Category:** Author responded/deferred to a third party; core objection never resolved; **objection is standing in the shipped build.** No sign-off.

**Files:** Assets/Scripts/Managers/GameController.cs, Assets/Scripts/UI/LoseScreen.cs, Assets/Scripts/Helper/Memory.cs, Assets/Scripts/Ads/UI/MainMenuAdsController.cs

input.title: Combo-Fighters PR #35 merged (author self-merge) with reviewer's _statPrefab type-safety objection unaddressed
input.description:
Record of PR state (Combo Fighter is live). Recorded during the Feb 2026 pre-shutdown audit — unassigned by design; record of state, not a commitment to fix.

**PR:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters #35 "Blake/backend" (author Arthur Blake, **self-merged** 2026-01-30, ~6 min after his only reply).

**Reviewer:** Oliver Brooks — review state CHANGES_REQUESTED (4 inline comments). He never approved. Arthur merged his own PR.

**What the reviewer objected to (with substance):**
1. `Assets/Store/DominoPlayerPrefs.cs` — "Can we rename this to something else?" Arthur replied "Yes". **This one landed** — file was renamed to `HarmonyPlayerPrefs.cs` before merge. (Agreement kept.)
2. `Assets/Scripts/UI/Profile/ProfileScreen.cs` — "missing `private`". Appears addressed.
3. `Assets/Scripts/UI/Profile/ProfileScreen.cs` — `_statPrefab` is a `GameObject` that is instantiated then `GetComponent<ProfileStat>()`'d; Oliver: *"Looks dangerous... make `_statPrefab` a `ProfileStat` instead of a GameObject so you force the prefab to have a ProfileStat and can remove the null check + GetComponent."* Raised twice ("Same thing"). **NOT done** — shipped code still uses `GameObject _statPrefab` + `Instantiate` + `GetComponent`; only a null-guard `Debug.LogError` was added. The author never replied to these two comments — just merged. Leftover `Debug.Log("AddStat(...)")` diagnostics also shipped.

**Also (context, bot not teammate):** CodeRabbit flagged security issues in `Assets/AWSGameSDK/AWSGameSDKClient.cs` — logging `rawResponse`/auth tokens on login error, no URL-encoding of GET params, and several silent login-failure paths. These are unaddressed in a backend-auth PR on a live money-taking title. Not a human review, but worth a look given the sensitivity.

**Category:** Mixed — the rename was agreed AND landed; the `_statPrefab` type-safety objection was **ignored and merged** (author didn't argue it, just merged). No sign-off.

input.title: Combo-Fighters PR #37 merged without sign-off; ComboRarityDefinition shipped as unused stub not backed by any design spec
input.description:
Record of PR state (Combo Fighter is live). Recorded during the Feb 2026 pre-shutdown audit — unassigned by design; record of state, not a commitment to fix.

**PR:** harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters #37 "Combo Definition Updates" (author PERSON_5877, merged by Oliver Brooks 2026-02-13).

**Reviewer:** Oliver Brooks — review state CHANGES_REQUESTED (7 inline comments). He never clicked Approve, but merged it himself.

**What the reviewer asked, and what actually landed (verified against the merged branch):**
- `ComboDefinition.cs` `Locked` should not be a stored SO field → **fixed** (now `IsLocked => !ComboManager.Instance.IsComboUnlocked(Id)`).
- `LevelMultiplierRow` class unnecessary → **fixed** (row class removed; leveling now via `ComboLevelUpData`).
- enum should be `E`-prefixed → **fixed** (`ERarityEnum`; note `Common` was also dropped from the enum).
- `_specialPrefab` naming → author argued it also covers non-locked/unlocked combos; shipped as `SpecialComboCell` (author's position, reasonable).
- per-rarity display via `SerializedDictionary` instead of per-rarity functions → **fixed**.
- **`ComboRarityDefinition` — "Why exactly do we need this?"** The author justified it in-review by citing "Combo Unlocking Specs" (per-rarity, per-level requirement rows: Common 100/200/300, Rare 150/300/450). **What shipped is a bare `public int LevelRequirements;`** — a single int that implements none of the described table and is not consumed by the leveling path (`ComboDefinition` uses `ComboLevelUpData`, not this SO). It is effectively an orphaned stub.

**Design check:** The cited "Combo Unlocking Specs" does not exist as a written spec. Neither the Combo Fighter GDD (§9 "Combo List and their Bonus Multipliers") nor the master "Combo Fighter Design Details" spreadsheet contains a combo rarity system, unlock costs, or a per-rarity/per-level unlock-requirement table. The rarity tiers were being defined live in the #prototype Slack channel on 2026-02-12/13 — the same days as this review. So the whole rarity/unlock/leveling system shipped ahead of (and without) a design spec backing it.

**Category:** Author argued the point and most code objections were resolved in-branch — **so note that the code got fixed anyway.** Remaining: `ComboRarityDefinition` shipped as an unused stub justified by a non-existent spec, and the PR merged with no formal sign-off.

**Audit note (Feb 2026 pre-shutdown state record) — unresolved review objection.**

This PR merged 2026-01-15 while the reviewer's review was still in **CHANGES_REQUESTED**; there was no subsequent approval before merge.

The standing objection is not a nit. In the review, Oliver Brooks flagged a monetization exploit: because the upgrade-ad cooldown is reset on the lose screen as well as on level completion (`GameController.cs` and `LoseScreen.cs` both call `Memory.SetUpgradeAdWatchedCooldown(reset: true)`), a player can *"enter the level, lose very quickly and return to main menu and then watch another ad and level up again,"* defeating the 5-minute cooldown. The shipped code still resets on loss, so this is live. The author deferred to a teammate ("does not matter if the player win or lose... we should sync") and the PR merged without that being resolved or re-reviewed.

Recorded as **ENG-2438** so it survives past Slack. No fix committed — this is a record of state.

input.body:
**Audit note (Feb 2026 pre-shutdown state record) — merged without formal sign-off; one item unresolved + not backed by spec.**

This PR merged 2026-02-13 while the review was in **CHANGES_REQUESTED**. No Approve was ever clicked (it was merged by the reviewer himself). To be fair to the record: **most of the reviewer's points were actually addressed on the branch before merge** —
- `Locked` no longer a stored SO field → now computed (`IsLocked => !ComboManager.Instance.IsComboUnlocked(Id)`). ✅
- `LevelMultiplierRow` class removed; leveling moved to `ComboLevelUpData`. ✅
- enum renamed to `ERarityEnum` (and `Common` dropped from it). ✅
- per-rarity visuals moved to a `SerializedDictionary` instead of per-rarity functions. ✅
- `_specialPrefab` naming — author argued it also covers non-locked combos; kept as `SpecialComboCell` (reasonable). ✅

**The one that did not hold up:** `ComboRarityDefinition`. The reviewer asked *"Why exactly do we need this?"* and the author justified it by citing the **"Combo Unlocking Specs"** (per-rarity, per-level requirement rows — Common 100/200/300, Rare 150/300/450). What actually shipped is `public int LevelRequirements;` — a single int that implements none of that table and isn't consumed by the leveling path. It's effectively an orphaned stub.

**Design check:** that cited spec doesn't exist in written form. Neither the Combo Fighter GDD (§9) nor the master "Combo Fighter Design Details" sheet defines combo rarities, unlock costs, or a per-rarity/per-level unlock-requirement table. Those tiers were being decided live in #prototype on 2026-02-12/13 — the same days as this review.

Recorded as **ENG-2440**. Record of state, no fix committed.

**Audit note (Feb 2026 pre-shutdown state record) — merged without formal sign-off; one item unresolved + not backed by spec.**

This PR merged 2026-02-13 while the review was in **CHANGES_REQUESTED**. No Approve was ever clicked (it was merged by the reviewer himself). To be fair to the record: **most of the reviewer's points were actually addressed on the branch before merge** —
- `Locked` no longer a stored SO field → now computed (`IsLocked => !ComboManager.Instance.IsComboUnlocked(Id)`). ✅
- `LevelMultiplierRow` class removed; leveling moved to `ComboLevelUpData`. ✅
- enum renamed to `ERarityEnum` (and `Common` dropped from it). ✅
- per-rarity visuals moved to a `SerializedDictionary` instead of per-rarity functions. ✅
- `_specialPrefab` naming — author argued it also covers non-locked combos; kept as `SpecialComboCell` (reasonable). ✅

**The one that did not hold up:** `ComboRarityDefinition`. The reviewer asked *"Why exactly do we need this?"* and the author justified it by citing the **"Combo Unlocking Specs"** (per-rarity, per-level requirement rows — Common 100/200/300, Rare 150/300/450). What actually shipped is `public int LevelRequirements;` — a single int that implements none of that table and isn't consumed by the leveling path. It's effectively an orphaned stub.

**Design check:** that cited spec doesn't exist in written form. Neither the Combo Fighter GDD (§9) nor the master "Combo Fighter Design Details" sheet defines combo rarities, unlock costs, or a per-rarity/per-level unlock-requirement table. Those tiers were being decided live in #prototype on 2026-02-12/13 — the same days as this review.

Recorded as **ENG-2440**. Record of state, no fix committed.

input.text:
Arthur — Combo Fighter PR audit done (repo: harmonygames-Games/Combo-Fighters, 37 PRs, last activity Feb 13). Written record below. For every one I flagged I left a comment on the PR itself and raised one ENG ticket (no bundling), all unassigned. Reviewer throughout is Oliver Brooks; CodeRabbit is a bot, not counted as a teammate.

═══ FLAGGED — merged with a human reviewer's objection and NO sign-off ═══

▸ PR #26 "Added cooldown to main menu upgrade ad watch"  →  ENG-2438
Oliver's review (CHANGES_REQUESTED, never approved) flagged a real monetization exploit, not a nit: the upgrade-ad cooldown is reset on the lose screen as well as on level-complete (GameController.cs + LoseScreen.cs both call Memory.SetUpgradeAdWatchedCooldown(reset:true)), so a player can enter a level, lose fast, bounce to menu and watch another ad to level up again — defeating the 5-min cooldown.
What actually landed: the reset-on-loss is still in the shipped code, so the hole is live. Author deferred to a teammate ("doesn't matter if they win or lose... we should sync") and it merged unresolved.
→ Category: author responded/deferred, objection never resolved, **standing in the build.**

▸ PR #35 "Blake/backend" (you authored it; you also self-merged it ~6 min after the one reply)  →  ENG-2439
Oliver CHANGES_REQUESTED, 4 inline, never approved. Checked each against what shipped:
 • rename DominoPlayerPrefs.cs → you said "Yes" and it DID land (now HarmonyPlayerPrefs.cs). ✅
 • "missing private" on ProfileScreen → addressed. ✅
 • ProfileScreen._statPrefab: Oliver twice said the GameObject+GetComponent pattern is dangerous, make it a typed ProfileStat → **not done**, still GameObject+Instantiate+GetComponent, only a null-guard added. No reply, just merged. Leftover Debug.Log("AddStat…") diagnostics shipped too. ❌
 • Context (bot, not a teammate, but it's your live backend): CodeRabbit flagged AWSGameSDKClient.cs logging auth tokens/rawResponse on login error, no URL-encoding of GET params, silent login failures — none addressed.
→ Category: one point agreed+landed; the type-safety objection **ignored and merged.**

▸ PR #37 "Combo Definition Updates"  →  ENG-2440
Oliver CHANGES_REQUESTED, 7 inline, never clicked Approve — but he merged it himself. Being fair to the record: most of his points WERE fixed on the branch before merge — Locked made a computed property, LevelMultiplierRow class removed, enum renamed ERarityEnum, per-rarity visuals moved to a SerializedDictionary, _specialPrefab kept as SpecialComboCell after the author argued it. So on those, the code got fixed anyway.
The one that didn't hold up: ComboRarityDefinition. Oliver asked "why do we need this?" and the author justified it by pointing at "Combo Unlocking Specs" (per-level rows: Common 100/200/300, Rare 150/300/450). What shipped is a bare `public int LevelRequirements;` — a single int that implements none of that and isn't even consumed by the leveling path. Orphaned stub, merged with no sign-off.

═══ CLEAN — reviewer signed off before merge (leave alone) ═══
▸ PR #24 "AppLovinMAX integration and Rewarded Ads": Oliver CHANGES_REQUESTED twice, author fixed the points (removed unused popup params, removed the impossible FTUE-death branch after Oliver confirmed it), Oliver then **APPROVED at 20:08 before the 20:14 merge.** That's the process working — no action.

═══ The split you asked for ═══
• Author came back and argued the point: #37 (argued and largely delivered), #26 (deferred to a teammate).
• Nobody said a word — reviewer ignored: #35's _statPrefab objection (merged with no response).
• Agreed to a change then it never landed (the "looks settled but isn't" case): **none found.** The one clear agreement — your "Yes" to the DominoPlayerPrefs rename in #35 — actually landed.
• Also worth knowing: several PRs (#28, #33, #27, #8, #3) merged with a reviewer *requested but never given* — zero review, not an ignored objection, but they went in unreviewed.

═══ Design check (you asked me to verify the spec) ═══
Your memory is right to be uneasy. The "Combo Unlocking Specs" cited in the #37 review does not exist as a written spec. Neither the Combo Fighter GDD (§9 is just "Combo List and their Bonus Multipliers") nor the master "Combo Fighter Design Details" sheet defines combo rarities, unlock costs, or any per-rarity/per-level unlock-requirement table. The rarity tiers (Rare/Epic/Legendary/Mythic, Common dropped) were being hashed out right here in #prototype on Feb 12–13 — the same days as that review. So the rarity/unlock/leveling system shipped ahead of a spec, and the spec doesn't say what was claimed in the review.

═══ Zombie Match board ═══
You were right that there's urgent stuff sitting open (6 priority-Urgent tickets still open: ZOM-611, ZOM-608, ZOM-667, ZOM-438, ZOM-591, ZOM-535). But I could NOT confirm any of them actually shipped/were fixed — no resolution notes, no comments, and no matching Done/duplicate ticket for any of them. They're all live-service bug reports (card-sync loss, lives-sync, black-screen startup, screen flicker, spawn bugs), so I did NOT close them on a guess — closing a live bug wrongly buries it. Two of them (ZOM-438, ZOM-535) are about the old "zombie" mechanic you're pivoting away from, so those may be obsolete rather than shipped — your call. Happy to close specific ones if you can point me at where they landed.

One tooling note: the PR-comment endpoint on #26 posted fine; #35 and #37 I had to post as review-comments (the plain comment endpoint threw a DB id collision) — same content, on the PRs.

Done. Here's what I did, following Arthur's instructions to the letter.

## What Arthur asked for (from #prototype)
A written record of what actually landed in the **Combo-Fighters** repo and its state, PRs merged over an unresolved reviewer objection, with substance (files + what was asked), split by how the objection died, checking what *actually landed on the branch* rather than the review status — plus a PR comment + one unassigned ENG ticket per flag, a Zombie Match cleanup, and the summary posted back in that channel.

## Flags (merged with a human reviewer's objection, no sign-off)
Reviewer throughout is **Oliver Brooks**. Each got a PR comment + one ENG ticket.

- **PR #26** → **ENG-2438** — Oliver flagged a real ad-cooldown *exploit* (cooldown resets on loss too, so lose-fast → rewatch ad → level up again). The reset-on-loss **is in the shipped code**. Author deferred to a teammate; merged unresolved.
- **PR #35** (your own PR, self-merged ~6 min after one reply) → **ENG-2439** — the `DominoPlayerPrefs` rename you agreed to *did* land (`HarmonyPlayerPrefs.cs`); the `_statPrefab` type-safety objection was **ignored and merged** (still `GameObject`+`GetComponent`). Bonus: CodeRabbit's token-logging/URL-encoding flags on the live backend are unaddressed.
- **PR #37** → **ENG-2440** — *most* of Oliver's points were genuinely fixed on the branch (so the ticket says so), but `ComboRarityDefinition`, which the author defended by citing the "Combo Unlocking Specs," shipped as an orphaned `int LevelRequirements;` stub, no sign-off.

**Clean (left alone):** PR #24 — Oliver approved before merge. The process worked.

## The split
- **Argued the point:** #37 (and delivered most of it), #26 (deferred to a teammate).
- **Nobody said a word / ignored:** #35's `_statPrefab`.
- **Agreed then never landed (the worst kind):** **none** — the one agreement (your rename) actually landed.

## Design check
Your instinct was right: the **"Combo Unlocking Specs" doesn't exist in writing.** Neither the GDD nor the master Design Details sheet defines rarities, unlock costs, or the per-level requirement table that was cited in the review. Those tiers were being decided live in #prototype the same two days as the review.

## Zombie Match
6 urgent tickets are open (ZOM-611/608/667/438/591/535) but **none had any evidence they shipped** — no resolution notes, no matching Done ticket. They're live-service bug reports, so I did **not** close them on a guess and asked Arthur to point me at where any landed if he wants them closed.

Everything is recorded in the three tickets, the PR comments, and the summary posted in #prototype.

One heads-up: the plain PR-comment endpoint hit a DB id collision, so #35 and #37 notes went up as review-comments instead (same content, on the PRs); #26 posted normally.
